claims.value: other: sheath wrapped around a single axon segment
claims.quote: Oligodendrocytes have processes that reach out to multiple axon segments, whereas the entire Schwann cell surrounds just one axon segment.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.quote: For Schwann cells, the outermost layer of the cell membrane contains cytoplasm and the nucleus of the cell as a bulge on one side of the myelin sheath.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.quote: Outside the plasma membrane of the axon is the myelin sheath, which is composed of the tightly wrapped plasma membrane of a Schwann cell.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: myelin layers: the cell wraps around the axon several times, with little to no cytoplasm between the layers
claims.quote: The glial cell is wrapped around the axon several times with little to no cytoplasm between the glial cell layers.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: outer bulge on one side of the myelin sheath holding the cytoplasm and nucleus
claims.quote: For Schwann cells, the outermost layer of the cell membrane contains cytoplasm and the nucleus of the cell as a bulge on one side of the myelin sheath.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: The Schwann cell insulates axons in the peripheral nervous system by covering them with myelin.
claims.quote: The second type of glial cell is the Schwann cell, which insulate axons with myelin in the periphery.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: Because the entire Schwann cell surrounds the axon, each Schwann cell provides myelin for only one axon.
claims.quote: This is distinctive from the PNS where a single Schwann cell provides myelin for only one axon as the entire Schwann cell surrounds the axon.

source.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: Schwann cells wrap axons of the peripheral nervous system, either myelinating them or simply ensheathing them.
claims.quote: A glial cell that myelinates or ensheathes axons in the peripheral nervous system.

claims.value: Its myelin is a lipid-rich sheath around the axon that helps electrical signals travel along the axon.
claims.quote: Myelin is a lipid-rich sheath that surrounds the axon and by doing so creates a myelin sheath that facilitates the transmission of electrical signals along the axon.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

tier1.text: A glial cell that myelinates or ensheathes axons in the peripheral nervous system.
